narrative.synopsis: [Sidenote: Charon.] The cloud myths, to which frequent allusion has already been made, comprise not only the cattle of the sun, the Centaurs, Nephele, Phryxus, Helle, and Pegasus Her many children, the mists, are fully as beautiful as Apollo and Diana, by whose bright darts they are ruthlessly slain.

As the ancient Aryan had the same word to denote cloud and mountain ("for the piles of vapor on the horizon were so like Alpine ranges"), the cloud and mountain myths are often the same. In the story of Niobe we have one of the cloud myths.

events.sourceSentence: [Sidenote: Charon.] The cloud myths, to which frequent allusion has already been made, comprise not only the cattle of the sun, the Centaurs, Nephele, Phryxus, Helle, and Pegasus, but as, "in primitive Aryan lore, the sky itself was a blue sea, and the clouds were ships sailing over it," so Charon's boat was supposed to be one of these vessels, and the gilded shallop in which the sun daily made his pilgrimage back to the far east, another.
